messages:
emily: heads-up: after the 12:00 deploy, canary is failing p95->5xx spike on /v1/generate. PagerDuty fired. tagging oncall.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: INC-7890 - canary: deploy v2026.02.12 -> 5xx rate > 4% on region-us-east (auto-escalation enabled)
kai: @emily seeing it in dashboards too — errors start ~ 12:02, p50 fine but p95/99 spiking. rolling canary ~10% traffic.
oncall-bot: @kai, you are primary oncall (rotation: kai). Please acknowledge the incident in PagerDuty.
kai: acked in PD :white_check_mark: — I'm on it.
sre-lead: joining. quick ask: are these 5xx from model runtime OOM or upstream auth? logs?
emily: initial trace looks like a model runtime kernel error, stacktrace shows segfaults in quantized path. sample log:
```
2026-02-12T12:02:15Z worker-7 ERROR shard-3 model_runtime: runtime_error: segfault at kernel quant_mm_sparse
trace id: d8f3a2
```
jess: rolling canary at 10% — suggest divert traffic to stable and pause rollout. I'll prepare rollback plan. canary group id: canary-2026-02-12.
devon: quick mitigation: toggle routing policy to route canary -> 0% (instant drop) and fallback to stable-model-v3. command:
```
redwood route update --service inference --canary canary-2026-02-12 --weight 0
redwood route update --service inference --variant stable-model-v3 --weight 100
```
kai: doing the route change now (ETA ~30s)
kai: route change applied :rocket: — traffic to canary read 0% in control plane at 12:05:02.
pagerduty-bot: Alert status: acknowledged by kai. Auto-escalation paused for 15m.
cs-lead: quick heads-up — CS is getting pings from 2 enterprise customers in us-east about timeouts. ticket numbers: #C-442, #C-443. impact appears retries -> increased latency for chat flow, some failed requests.
sre-lead: thanks. we should still rollback the canary release. jess, can you kick the rollback and confirm commit hash to revert to?
jess: initiating rollback to stable commit: a1b2c3d. running rollback job:
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=stable-a1b2c3d
```
jess: rollback started at 12:07:10. watching pod events.
emily: switching observability alerts to reduced sensitivity for canary metric to avoid noisy churn during rollback.
kai: pods for canary replaced, new pods coming up, dtrace shows errors dropping. raw 5xx rate down from 4.3% -> 0.6% within 90s.
devon: confirmed KV cache warmups ok. fallback model variant stable-model-v3 serving tokens normally.
cs-lead: notified affected customers with note: "We detected an anomalous increase in errors during a canary rollout at 12:02. We diverted traffic and rolled back; service stability restored. Follow-up: postmortem and mitigation." they want ETA for RCA.
pagerduty-bot: Alert: resolved by user kai at 12:09:15. Incident state: resolved. Acknowledgements closed.
oncall-bot: handing off to postmortem owner assignment. Suggested owner: @jess (release engineer) + @sre-lead for RCA. Please file postmortem within 72h.
sre-lead: agreed. initial hypothesis: quantized runtime kernel regression introduced by model build path for canary. next steps: preserve failing pods, collect core dumps, instrument reproducer with same weights/quant flags.
jess: I saved pod logs and core dump blobs to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-7890/ and will open an RFC for blocking the quant path until we patch. Also will add a gate to rollout for kernel-smoke-tests.
emily: reassigning follow-ups: jess (owner), devon (routing policy test), kai (monitoring signal tuning). I'll open the incident thread in the tracker.
cs-lead: customers acknowledged, they've escalated to priority but are satisfied with rollback update for now.
emily: thanks everyone — locking this thread. we'll post the postmortem link when created. :lock:
